Qiskit Fall Fest 2026 Warsaw · Track 2 Quantum machine learning · Question

Does time-crystal order give a quantum reservoir better memory, and does any of it beat classical models on real data?

Quantum reservoir computing (Fujii & Nakajima 2017): let a disordered quantum system evolve, feed the input in, measure, and train only a linear readout. The physics does the feature engineering.

Discrete time crystals are driven spin chains that flip with period 2T and resist perturbations. Zhang et al. (2025) built a time-crystal reservoir and found phase boundaries best on synthetic tasks.

What we ask

  • Which Floquet phase gives the most memory: time-crystal, scrambling, or weakly kicked?
  • Does the best-memory phase also forecast real series best?
  • Does it beat an echo-state network, a linear AR model and persistence with the same features, splits and readout?
  • What would measurement cost on hardware?

Data (small, real, public; bundled with statsmodels)

SeriesValuesTrainValTest
Sunspots (yearly)3092004762
Mauna Loa CO₂ (monthly change)52534179105

Yearly sunspot number 1700–2008 (309 values, statsmodels). Mauna Loa CO2, monthly change 1958–2001 (525 values, statsmodels). Time-ordered splits, train 65 % / validation 15 % / test 20 %.

Short answer

Time-crystal order hurts memory: it freezes the spins. The scrambling regime remembers as much as an 11-node ESN, but on real forecasting a linear AR model wins both series.

Qiskit Fall Fest 2026 Warsaw · Track 2 Quantum machine learning · Model

A 6-spin kicked Ising chain, reset-and-inject input, 11 measured features

Circuit drawing: one step, one Floquet cycle, θ = 0.95π shown. The disorder angles hi are drawn per seed.

1 · Injectreset qubit 0 to √(1−u)|0⟩ + √u|1⟩
2 · Evolve2 Floquet cycles per step
3 · Read⟨Zi⟩ and ⟨ZiZi+1⟩

Floquet cycle UF = e−i Σ hiZi e−i J Σ ZiZi+1 Π Rx(θ), disorder hi ~ U[−π, π].

  • θ ≈ π, J ≠ 0: time crystal (period-doubled magnetisation).
  • θ ≈ π/2: scrambling (thermalising) kicks.
  • J = 0: no interactions; information cannot leave qubit 0. Our quantum control.

Readout: 6 + 5 = 11 features → ridge regression. Only the readout is trained.

Simulated exactly with NumPy density matrices (26 × 26). One reservoir step is cross-checked against Qiskit Aer's density-matrix simulator in tests/.

Track 2 brief → what we did

  • Real datasets, kept small (309 and 525 values).
  • Same 11 features (or fewer) and the same split for every model.
  • Min–max scaled on the training block only, not clipped (a test checks it).
  • All hyperparameters chosen on validation; test touched once.
  • Cross-validated: 8 seeds, plus 4-fold rolling-origin CV.
  • Shows where the classical model wins, with Diebold–Mariano tests per seed.

Qiskit Fall Fest 2026 Warsaw · Track 2 Quantum machine learning · Result 1 · memory

Time-crystal order hurts memory: it freezes the spins

  • Scrambling kicks remember. With J = 0.4, memory capacity is ≥ 5 for θ = 0.35π–0.65π, peaking at 5.75 (θ = 0.45π). That is inside the 11-node ESN range (5.31–7.82).
  • The time crystal forgets. At θ = 0.95π the chain is strongly period-doubled (order 0.97) and memory capacity is only 1.32: the spins mostly flip back and forth, and the input barely spreads.
  • Across the scan, memory capacity anti-correlates with time-crystal order (r = -0.51, J ∈ {0.4, π/4}).
  • J = 0 control stays at 0.57–1.07 at every θ: without interactions there is no reservoir.
  • 11 raw lags would score 11.00: a linear delay line is the memory ceiling.

20 kick angles × 3 couplings × 5 disorder seeds; mean ± s.d. shaded.

Each fold moves the test block forward and re-tunes every model on its own preceding validation block; per-fold numbers are medians over seeds.

Sunspots (yearly)7 / 86 / 80 / 80 / 8

Full ranking (median test NMSE)

Sunspots: AR 0.13 < ESN 0.17 < Quantum reservoir 0.38 < Persistence 0.39 < J = 0 control 0.42

CO₂: AR 0.11 < ESN 0.13 < Quantum reservoir 0.21 < J = 0 control 0.49 < Persistence 0.57

Why classical wins here

  • Both series are close to linear-autoregressive. Sunspots have an ~11-year cycle; CO₂ changes have a 12-month cycle. AR with p ≈ 10–11 lags captures exactly that, and our reservoir remembers only ~6 steps.
  • An 11-node ESN has the same feature count, more memory than the best quantum phase, and costs microseconds.
  • Reservoir choice is fragile on sunspots: θ picked on validation varies by seed (0.5π ×2, 0.65π ×4, 0.8π ×2).

What the quantum reservoir does show: interactions matter. On CO₂ the J = 0 control is 2.4× worse, so the forecasting skill comes from many-body dynamics, not the single-qubit encoding.

θ = 0.5π, J = 0.4; mean over seeds.

The time crystal is shot-robust only because it has almost no memory to lose.

Hardware: a projective readout destroys the state, so the sequence is re-run up to every readout time: 95,790 Floquet cycles per shot for the 309-year sunspot series instead of 618 (155×), and 309,000 circuit runs at 1,000 shots. Our whole E2 protocol would need ≈ 40 million runs. Windowed replay or weak measurement (Mujal et al. 2023) would cut this.

An independent replication and extension, not the first time-crystal reservoir

WorkReservoirFinding
Fujii & Nakajima 2017disordered spinsQRC; reset-and-inject input
Martínez-Peña et al. PRL 2021static disordered Isingthermal phase / transition best; localisation hurts
Mujal et al. 2023measurement protocolsrestart / weak-measurement cost set by memory time
Zhang et al. 2025 (arXiv:2508.15230)DTC kicked Ising, same input and readoutphase boundaries best on memory, parity, NARMA10; MNIST on hardware

Zhang et al. is the closest work and essentially our model. Our scan was done independently; see docs/literature.md.

What this project adds

  • Real series: sunspots and CO₂, not only synthetic tasks.
  • Matched classical baselines: an ESN with the same 11 features, linear AR, persistence, and a J = 0 quantum control, all tuned on validation only.
  • Memory phase ≠ forecasting phase: on sunspots the validation-best θ does not hold on test.
  • Measurement cost: shot noise and restart bill per phase.

Consistent with prior work: deep in the time-crystal phase the reservoir is a poor memory; the useful regime is the scrambling side, toward the boundary.

Qiskit Fall Fest 2026 Warsaw · Track 2 Quantum machine learning · Takeaways

Time-crystal order is robust because it does not listen

  • Memory: scrambling kicks reach ESN-level memory (5.75); the time crystal stays at 1.32.
  • Forecasting: linear AR wins both real series; the ESN is second; the quantum reservoir is third and beats its J = 0 control.
  • Hardware: with 1,000 shots the scrambling advantage shrinks to 2.64, and every readout needs a restart.
  • No quantum advantage claimed. The useful output is a fair, reusable benchmark for the next reservoir idea.
